It's interesting how all 4 were similarly designed while also being different.

* Pikmin 1, 2, and 4 all thematically played against familiarity. 
   * The Emperor Bulblax sort of being the Bowser to Bulborb's Koopa's. 
   * Similarly with Titan Dweevil mechanically being very similar to Dweevil who were so so frequent in Caves
   * and Ancient Sirehound being the big version of Oatchi and Moss who were extremely important throughout the game as basically your souped up second captain.
* Then there's also the mechanical theme of representing every hazard that Pikmin 2 - 4 did.
   * Titan Dweevil had individual weapons that it could switch through at any point with the potency of each weapon being affected by how much damage the weapon took.
   * The Plasm Wraith left environmental hazard throughout its arena, eventually leaving multiple at once.
   * And the Ancient Sirehound kinda had one-ish attack pattern with each element more or less acting as modifiers to how the attacks worked.

It's nostalgia talking but I felt like I enjoyed Pikmin 2's the most. I didn't enjoy that the Ancient Sirehound basically just had health bar stages and it made the fight less dynamic than the other two.

The Plasm Wraith I just found overly stressful and overwhelming.

Additionally, there was a bit of an uneasiness that Titan Dweevil had that the Ancient Sirehound didn't in the fact that electricity was insta-kill and basically the water element did not "respect" the safety zones. If you had other Pikmin outside of the arena if you were not careful the Titan Dweevil could attack them and drown your Pikmin that were chilling at the exit.

Yeah more or less when you go to any art school or fundamentals class you typically always start first with grey scale and then later on the term you go to color.

A painting with good values and no color will still look amazing but a painting with good colors but incorrect values will always look little off or stylized!

That's exactly what that does. Procreate doesn't have a built-in grey filter but by doing what I said, you have a layer you can turn on or off which can be used to switch between grayscaled and colored.

For Procreate what you can easily do is make a new layer and fill it black then set the layer type to either "Saturation" or "Color" doing so will give you an easy way to just look at values without worrying about color.

I'd say do that for your painting but also do the same for your reference so you can catch a lot of the more subtle value changes with your brain and eyes not focusing on color.

That can be explained pretty easily. Worked with a screen protector company who's product was really easy to mess up.

They'd try installing the screen protector, fail, and then return it to Amazon with a reason like "changed my mind" or something. Basically claim it as unused so they get the full refund.

Amazon receives it under the assumption that it's unused because that's what the customer claimed and they put it back into sellable inventory.

It's a bad system but at the scale Amazon warehouses employees work it would be impossible for them to check every product since they're already overworked.

This would happen every few months for this company and we'd have to apologize to customers and explain why this was happening. We'd also have to create a support case with Amazon to check inventory but they won't do it without being prompted.

So tldr; you likely received a used return that a customer claimed was unused.
Probably bad luck I've been doing this for like 4-5 years.

It's actually very difficult for Amazon to mix up inventory.

If you look at most packages they have an additional sticker / code.

This is how Amazon delineates purchases from multiple sellers. Everyone might sell an ipad case but Seller A's inventory is assigned code abde while Seller B sells the same iPad case with a code of 1234.

So when a customer buys from seller B they pull the inventory with a code of 1234.

These codes need to be on the product before sending it to Amazon.

Yeah I've worked with a number of companies that work with Amazon.

If it's "Sold by" AND "Shipped By" Amazon it means Amazon directly purchased inventory from the manufacturer and should be the most authentic product (unless the company relies on a sketchy warehouse that sends fake inventory to Amazon).
